title: GPT (GUID Partition Table)
summary: GPT is the modern partition scheme. Layout: protective MBR (LBA 0), primary GPT header (LBA 1), partition entries (LBA 2-33, 128 entries × 128 bytes), data partitions, secondary partition entries, secondary GPT header (last LBA). GPT header: signature 'EFI PART' (8 bytes), revision (4), header size (4), CRC32 (4), reserved (4), current LBA (8), backup LBA (8), first usable LBA (8), last usable LBA (8), disk GUID (16), partition entries start LBA (8), number of entries (4), size of entry (4), CRC32 of entries (4).

structure.meaning: Legacy MBR with one partition of type 0xEE (GPT protective). Prevents old tools from misinterpreting the disk.
CRC32 of the header (with this field zeroed during computation).
LBA of the partition entry array.
Size of each partition entry (default 128 bytes).
CRC32 of the partition entry array.
Type GUID (16), unique GUID (16), first LBA (8), last LBA (8), attributes (8), name (72 bytes, UTF-16LE).

notes: GPT supports up to 128 partitions by default (configurable).
GPT uses 64-bit LBA → max 9.4 ZB (zettabytes) disk size.
GPT has a backup header at the end of the disk for recovery.
GPT partition types: C12A7328-F81F-11D2-BA4B-00A0C93EC93B (EFI System Partition), 0FC63DAF-8483-4772-8E79-3D69D8477DE4 (Linux filesystem), etc.
GPT is required for UEFI boot and disks > 2TB.
